comment: Single source of truth for URL redaction, decided in docs/adr/0003-redact-urls-in-logs.md (KEI-55). Redaction runs twice on the same line — once in src/redact.rs before the host emits a log event, once in extension/redact.js before the extension persists, broadcasts, or displays it — so both implementations must agree exactly. src/redact.rs's unit tests and tests/extension/redact.test.js both read this file, the way tests/fixtures/protocol.json pins the wire vocabulary. Every token here is a sentinel: nothing in this file is a real secret, and the tests grep for the sentinels to prove they do not survive.

cases.name: a plain URL with no query is left alone
the query of an FFmpeg segment line is replaced
a bare query, unquoted and at end of line
several URLs on one line are each redacted
a fragment is redacted too, because it can carry the same token
userinfo credentials are replaced, host and path kept
a port in the authority survives, because it is not a secret
http and HTTPS are both matched, whatever the case of the scheme
trailing sentence punctuation is not swallowed into the URL
cases.note: The trailing full stop belongs to the sentence. It is trimmed off the match and restored, so the placeholder does not absorb it.

cases.name: an empty query still loses its marker's contents
a scheme this product never downloads is left alone
cases.note: Only http and https are accepted by output.rs, so only those are matched. A query string elsewhere in the line is not assumed to be a URL.

cases.name: text with no URL at all passes through unchanged
cases.input: frame= 1234 fps= 60 q=-1.0 size=  12345kB time=00:01:23.45 bitrate=1234.5kbits/s
cases.expected: frame= 1234 fps= 60 q=-1.0 size=  12345kB time=00:01:23.45 bitrate=1234.5kbits/s
cases.note: FFmpeg's own progress vocabulary uses q= and size= freely. Redaction keys off the URL grammar, not off the presence of an equals sign.

cases.name: an error message, not a log line
the scheme alone is not a URL
cases.input: supported schemes are https:// and http://
cases.expected: supported schemes are https:// and http://
